notes: Miller, chapter IV, note 26: first name is variously given as Fusayasu, Seikichi, and Harukichi. This increment uses Harukichi, the form Miller adopts in the narrative.
Miller, chapter IV, writes Kiyono and notes that some translations render the name as Ikki. The Japanese given name 清直 is usually romanized Kiyonao.
Miller, chapter V, writes Akinosuka Oka as commander of the 124th Infantry.
Miller, chapter VI: commander of 17th Army artillery and of the October coast force west of the Matanikau.
Miller, chapter VI: commanded the left wing of the 2nd Division’s October envelopment (the 29th Infantry). Listed among the Japanese dead of that counter-offensive; day of death not copied.

Colonel. Took command of the 5th Marines on 21 September 1942 after Colonel Hunt departed (Miller, ch. V; Zimmerman, ch. VI). Commanded the combined Matanikau forces of 27 September and the 1–3 November Point Cruz attack.

Brigadier General (Major General in Appendix C as the highest rank held in the period). Commanded 1st Marine Aircraft Wing on Guadalcanal from 3 September 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Part VI, ch. 5 and Appendix C).
Colonel. Commanded Marine Aircraft Group 23 on Guadalcanal, 20 August–4 November 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Appendix C).
Major. Commanded VMF-223, the first Marine fighter squadron at Henderson Field, 20 August–16 October 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Part VI, ch. 4 and Appendix C; Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2).
Lieutenant Colonel. Commanded VMSB-232, the first Marine scout-bomber squadron at Henderson Field, 20 August–2 November 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Appendix C; Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2).
Major. Commanded VMF-224 at Henderson Field, 30 August–2 November 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Appendix C and Part VI, ch. 5).

Captain, later Major. Led the first 67th Fighter Squadron P-400s into Henderson Field on 22 August 1942; on 12 November brought in eight P-38s of the 339th Fighter Squadron (Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2).
Colonel. Commanded the 11th Bombardment Group at Espiritu Santo during the Guadalcanal campaign (Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2).
General (then Brigadier/Major General). First commander of Thirteenth Air Force; established headquarters on Espiritu Santo on 13 January 1943 (Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 3).
Brigadier General. Commanded the 2nd Marine Aircraft Wing forward echelon in the Guadalcanal area from 26 December 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Appendix C).
Lieutenant Colonel. Commanded MAG-14 in the Guadalcanal area from 16 October 1942 to 17 December 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Appendix C).
Vice Admiral. Commanded TF 61 at the Battle of the Eastern Solomons, 24 August 1942 (Cressman). Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.

Rear Admiral. Commanded the Enterprise group (TF 16) at Santa Cruz, 26 October 1942, and again on 13 November 1942 (Cressman). ONI Tassafaronga notes he first organized the Espiritu cruiser force later commanded by Wright. Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.
Rear Admiral. Commanded TF 17 (Hornet group) at Santa Cruz, 26 October 1942 (Cressman). Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.

Rear Admiral. Immediate commander of the August air-support force (ONI Landing, Task Force NEGAT) and of TF 18 when Wasp was torpedoed, 15 September 1942 (Cressman). Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.
Rear Admiral. Commanded TF 18 at the Battle of Rennell Island, 29-30 January 1943 (Cressman). Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.

Rear Admiral. Commanded TG 64.2 at Cape Esperance, 11-12 October 1942 (Cressman). Killed on board Atlanta in the Cruiser Night Action, 13 November 1942 (Cressman). Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.
Rear Admiral. Commanded TG 67.4 in the Cruiser Night Action of 12-13 November 1942; killed on board San Francisco (Cressman). Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.
Rear Admiral. Commanded TF 64 in the Battleship Night Action of 14-15 November 1942; flag in Washington (Cressman). Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.

Rear Admiral. Commanded TF 67 at Tassafaronga, 30 November 1942 (Cressman; ONI, which spells the given name Carleton). Cressman prints Carlton; the unit and person notes record both spellings, and the person name follows the ONI narrative of the force he took over in Minneapolis. Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.

Rear Admiral. Commanded the Amphibious Force in the 7-8 August landings (Cressman; ONI Task Force TARE) and TF 67 unloading in Lunga Roads on 12 November 1942 (Cressman). Branch guadalcanal-naval-pilot, 26 November 2026.
